newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber prices end mixed.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber prices end mixed.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices bucked a firm midday trend to close mixed, with traders blaming the poor finish on the continued absence of consumer demand.

The Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB) quoted benchmark April RSS1 buyer at 306 cents ($1.24) a kg at the close, down half cent from Thursday. The board quoted April SMR20 buyer was half cent higher at 293 cents a kg.
Traders offered the SMR20 at 293 cents a kg, SMR CV at 358, SMR L at 338, SMR 5 at 304, SMR 10 at 294 and latex at 237.
Traders said with the absence of demand and local leads, domestic prices were basically taking their cue from the Tokyo market.
"Hopefully, we'll see some demand by next week," said a trader.
Poor demand for spot rubber has made producers bank on forward orders for June/July/August, traders said.
The INRO five-day average was at 232.39 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on March 13 from 232.44 cents per kg on Mar 12. The daily indicator was at 231.99 from 232.55 previously.
